text:
rachel: Hey team — quick logistics Q. I'm heading to Berlin and need a Schengen visa. Can Redwood advance the visa fee and travel docs? Also curious about VAT reclaim rules and per-diem when I'm in-country for 6 nights.

 tom_people_ops: We can advance visa fees for trips that are business-approved. Submit a Travel Advance request in Concur (or the Travel Portal) with the visa invoice attached and tag People Ops. Finance will process the advance; you'll need to reconcile with receipts after the trip.

 rachel: Is there a max advance amount or timeline? The consulate asks for a 2-3 week lead time.

 tom_people_ops: Max advance for visa or pre-paid vendor fees is $1,500 by default. For exceptions (higher fees or group visas) route through your manager + People Ops for approval. Expect 5 business days processing for an advance once submitted with justification. For faster needs, mark as "expedite" and cc your manager.

 dan_manager: I'll pre-approve the trip and the visa advance. Rachel, include itinerary and confirmation of client meetings so finance can code the cost center.

 rachel: Thanks. On VAT: I paid VAT on a hotel and taxi in Berlin. Can Redwood reclaim that?

 vat_bot: VAT reclaim depends on local rules and whether invoices are in company name. If you have a vendor invoice with Redwood Inc. listed as the payer (or invoice that can be reissued), Finance can include it in VAT reclaim filings. Personal-card receipts in employee name are usually not eligible unless vendor issues a re-invoice to Redwood. Attach originals to expense and tag Finance for review.

 tom_people_ops: Practically: upload the hotel folio and any invoices. If it's personal card and vendor can't reissue, Finance may still be able to file a reclaim in certain EU countries but it's less reliable.

 rachel: About per-diem: I'm in-country 6 nights with two half-days for travel. Do I claim per-diem or actuals?

 tom_people_ops: Redwood allows either per-diem or actual meal receipts, not both. For Germany we use the international flat-rate $120/day USD. Travel days (first/last) are prorated at 75% each. So for a 6-night trip typically you get: 75% (arrival day) + 4 full days + 75% (departure) = 5.5 days at the daily rate. If you prefer to submit actual receipts, go ahead — Finance will reimburse actuals up to policy limits.

 rachel: Any special rules for group dinners when vendor pays? Client covered dinners should be marked as "provided" and not claimed. For shared tabs, how do we split?

 tom_people_ops: Mark provided meals as provided in Expensify. For shared tabs, itemize the receipt and indicate Redwood's portion; attach a short note explaining allocation. Manager sign-off required for ambiguous splits.

 rachel: Lost receipt for a €12 tram ride — do I need the Lost Receipt Affidavit?

 tom_people_ops: Yes, use the Lost Receipt Affidavit in Expensify. For low amounts (<$20) we can accept a card statement line plus a brief manager attestation instead of the affidavit.

 finance_bot: Expensify: report "BER - client week - Rachel" created by rachel  status: needs manager approval. Processing after approval ~7 business days.

 rachel: One last Q  if Finance advances the visa fee and we later successfully reclaim VAT on the hotel charged to the advance, does that reduce my reimbursement?

 tom_people_ops: Any VAT or refunds recovered that are attributable to your trip will be reconciled. If Finance recovers VAT that was originally paid via an advance or reimbursement, we will deduct the recovered amount from the final reimbursement during reconciliation and notify you. Keep all original invoices to speed this up.

 rachel: Great, I'll submit the travel advance and upload invoices as I get them. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
